# NC Structured Sentencing Supervision Length

> **Educational only, NOT legal advice.** For specific legal matters, consult a licensed North Carolina attorney.

`verified-as-of: 2026-06-22`

## Overview

North Carolina's structured sentencing framework under **GS 15A-1342** and **GS 15A-1343.2** establishes specific probation length ranges by offense class and punishment type. Probation length is determined by whether the sentence is community or intermediate punishment and whether the offense is a felony or misdemeanor. The **5-year maximum** applies to all felony probation; misdemeanor probation has a lower ceiling.[^1]

The most common sentencing error in NC is imposing probation outside the statutory range without the required written judicial findings justifying the extended term.[^3]

## Statutory Framework: Two Layers

### Layer 1: GS 15A-1342 — The Ceiling

GS 15A-1342 establishes the **maximum probation periods**:[^1]

| Defendant Category | Maximum Probation Period |
|-------------------|--------------------------|
| Convicted felony or misdemeanor offenders | **5 years** |
| Deferred prosecution or conditional discharge | **2 years** |
| Extension (with defendant consent) | Up to **3 additional years** beyond original period |

The court must also impose a suspended sentence alongside probation, which can be activated if probation conditions are violated (GS 15A-1344).

### Layer 2: GS 15A-1343.2 — Default Ranges

GS 15A-1343.2(d) establishes **default probation length ranges** for offenders sentenced under Structured Sentencing (post-October 1, 1994 offenses). These are the presumptive ranges — courts must stay within them OR make specific written findings justifying a longer term:[^1][^3]

#### Misdemeanor Offenders

| Punishment Type | Default Probation Range |
|----------------|------------------------|
| Community punishment | Not less than **6 months** nor more than **18 months** |
| Intermediate punishment | Not less than **12 months** nor more than **24 months** |

#### Felony Offenders

| Punishment Type | Default Probation Range |
|----------------|------------------------|
| Community punishment | Not less than **12 months** nor more than **30 months** |
| Intermediate punishment | Not less than **18 months** nor more than **36 months** |

**Absolute maximum:** Even with written findings, the probation period may not exceed **5 years** for convicted offenders, regardless of offense class.

## When Extended Terms Are Allowed

To impose probation exceeding the default range (up to the 5-year ceiling), the sentencing court must:[^3]
- Make specific **written findings** at sentencing that a longer period is necessary
- State the reason for exceeding the default range

**Failure to make written findings = improper probation period.** This is the most commonly litigated sentencing error in NC. In *State v. Wheeler*, the defendant received 24 months of community-punishment probation for a misdemeanor — exceeding the 18-month maximum without required judicial findings, making the sentence improper.[^3]

## Probation Extension (GS 15A-1342)

With the **defendant's written consent**, a court may extend an existing probation period:[^1]
- **When:** Only during the final 6 months of the original probation period
- **Maximum extension:** 3 additional years beyond the original period
- **Purposes:** Completing a program of restitution OR continuing medical/psychiatric treatment ordered as a probation condition
- **Hard cap:** Total probation including extension may not exceed 8 years (5-year max + 3-year extension)

## Deferred Prosecution and Conditional Discharge

Defendants whose prosecution is deferred or who receive a conditional discharge are placed on probation under different rules:[^1]
- Maximum probation period: **2 years**
- The 5-year felony maximum does not apply — 2 years is the absolute ceiling for these cases
- GS 15A-1342 also governs these cases

## Unsupervised Probation

Defendants placed on **unsupervised probation** are subject to the same length rules under GS 15A-1343.2 as supervised probation. The distinction is in the conditions, not the duration:[^2]

Unsupervised probationers are **not** subject to these standard conditions:
- Reporting to probation officer
- Allowing officer home visits
- Answering officer inquiries
- Not leaving state without permission (in certain circumstances)
- Drug testing
- Employment reporting
- Other specified officer-directed conditions

But duration rules (6-18 months for misdemeanor community, etc.) apply equally to supervised and unsupervised probation.

## Supervision Length vs. Post-Release Supervision

Probation length rules under GS 15A-1342 / GS 15A-1343.2 apply to **probation** — a suspended sentence served in the community. They do not govern:
- **Post-Release Supervision (PRS):** Automatically imposed on most felony offenders after release from an active prison term. PRS length is set by offense class under GS 15A-1368.2, not by these probation length statutes. See `nc-parole-commission-prspc`.
- **Special probation (split sentence):** Total probation including confinement still capped at 5 years under GS 15A-1343.2(d). See `nc-split-sentence-special-probation`.

## Summary Table

| Offense Category | Punishment Type | Default Range | Absolute Max |
|-----------------|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| Misdemeanor | Community | 6–18 months | 5 years (with findings) |
| Misdemeanor | Intermediate | 12–24 months | 5 years (with findings) |
| Felony | Community | 12–30 months | 5 years (with findings) |
| Felony | Intermediate | 18–36 months | 5 years (with findings) |
| Deferred prosecution / conditional discharge | Any | — | 2 years |
| Extension (with consent) | — | — | 3 additional years |

## Anti-Patterns / Common Mistakes

- **Imposing 24 months for a misdemeanor community punishment without written findings:** The default max is 18 months; 24 months requires specific written judicial findings. This is the most common NC sentencing error.[^3]
- **Assuming 5 years is always the felony max:** 5 years is the ceiling; the defaults are lower (12-30 months for community punishment, 18-36 months for intermediate punishment). Courts should stay within the default range unless findings justify going higher.
- **Confusing PRS length with probation length:** PRS is determined by offense class under different statutes; probation length under GS 15A-1342/1343.2 is determined by punishment type (community vs. intermediate) within the offense class.
- **Extending probation without defendant consent:** The 3-year extension option in GS 15A-1342 requires defendant written consent. A court cannot unilaterally extend probation beyond the original period except in limited circumstances.
- **Deferred prosecution defendants receiving 5-year probation:** The 2-year maximum applies specifically to deferred prosecution and conditional discharge cases — not the 5-year felony maximum.
